entries.test: Compare the commonsense problems identified in the authors' 2015 paper and 2019 book with publicly demonstrated AI capabilities as of January 2025.
entries.note: The referenced publications give the broad claim a concrete scope.

entries.test: Public evaluations of simulation, LLMs, and video generation would show whether any had achieved reliable commonsense reasoning by January 2025.
entries.note: In context, 'fully satisfactory' refers to solving the stated reasoning problems.

entries.test: Published evaluations and deployment records would show simulation's demonstrated success in commonsense reasoning compared with its established scientific, engineering, and entertainment applications.
Public household robotics evaluations and technical studies would show whether simulation-only physical reasoning is insufficient and contributes to the absence of general-purpose household robots.
entries.note: Rosie refers to a general-purpose domestic robot; the normalization broadens this to household robots doing any housework.
'Apparently' qualifies the attribution of all or most commonsense behavior to teleoperators.

entries.test: Retesting the cited GPT-3 examples and evaluating contemporary models on varied physical and spatial reasoning tasks would establish whether the old errors disappeared while broader failures persisted.
entries.note: The surrounding examples give 'robust understanding' a behavioral reading.

entries.test: Public controlled evaluations of o1 could establish the frequency of elementary spatial errors and whether failures in spatial reasoning explain them despite access to geometric calculation.
entries.note: This concerns operational model capabilities, rather than an inaccessible private belief.

entries.test: Public evaluations of models before and after fixes to individual commonsense examples would show whether new failures persist because those fixes fail to generalize.
Sora's public release records and reproducible video-generation tests would establish its availability and failures to depict ordinary physical interactions correctly in January 2025.

entries.note: The source says 'more like' collages than renderings, while the normalization makes the contrast categorical. The collage analogy and surreal quality lack a shared causal test.

entries.test: Public documentation of Sora's output representations and tests of object persistence and physical consistency would establish whether its outputs are unreliable image streams without explicit object-property segmentations.

entries.note: The source expresses weak grounds for believing in a possible capability, rather than forecasting its likelihood. The normalization turns evidential skepticism into an explicit probability claim.

entries.test: Public records of available agent capabilities in January 2025 and subsequent arrival of general-purpose domestic robots would test the present-capability and distant-arrival assertions.
entries.note: The source combines a future domestic-robot outlook with a present observation about agents. 'Already here to a limited degree' does not clearly assert the normalization's exclusive 'only'.

entries.test: AI companies' 2025 announcements, research programs, product launches, and industry coverage would establish whether agents were a major focus that year.
Public demonstrations of consistently successful agents, together with evaluations of their commonsense capabilities, would test whether agents can work well before major commonsense progress.
entries.note: The core prerequisite is asserted firmly. The possible need for wholesale revisions is separately hedged.

entries.test: TheAgentCompany results and comparable workplace evaluations would establish whether the tested agents reliably completed ordinary employee tasks as of January 2025.
entries.note: 'Ready for prime time' has a practical reliability meaning in this benchmark context.

entries.test: Public evaluations of agents operating reliably across real-world tasks would test whether such reliability can occur without commonsense competence about objects, people, and entities.
entries.note: The claim makes commonsense a necessary condition, not a sufficient one.

entries.test: Published evaluations across successive text- and video-trained models would show whether repeated attempts to obtain reliable commonsense through emergence had fallen short by January 2025.
entries.note: This describes the historical record, rather than asserting that future emergence is impossible.

entries.test: Public evaluations of contemporary AI systems on entity tracking, object properties, and physical interactions would establish whether recurring failures persisted as of January 2025.

entries.note: 'Begin to mature' supplies no shared outcome criterion, and 'grapple directly' leaves the prerequisite unclear.
